description_ru: История дочери поэта Байрона, которая написала первую в истории компьютерную программу ещё до появления компьютеров.
text:
Ada Lovelace was born in London in 1815. Her father was Lord Byron, a famous poet, but she hardly ever saw him because her parents separated soon after she was born. Her mother was afraid that Ada would become as wild as her father, so she made sure the girl studied mathematics and science instead of poetry.

As a teenager, Ada was clever and imaginative. She even tried to design a flying machine with wings. At the age of seventeen, she met Charles Babbage, an inventor who was building a huge mechanical calculator. He called it the Analytical Engine. The machine was never finished, yet Ada understood its power better than almost anyone.

In 1843 she translated an article about the engine from French into English. She added her own notes, which were three times longer than the article. In them, she explained how the machine could follow a list of instructions to solve a problem. Many historians believe this was the world's first computer program. She also predicted that machines might one day create music or art, an idea that seemed extraordinary at the time.

Ada died in 1852, when she was only thirty-six. Although she lived a short life, she saw the future more clearly than her friends did. If you use a computer today, you can thank her vision.

Верхние зубы касаются нижней губы, голос включён; не оглушайте звук до ф.
Округлите и вытяните губы вперёд, не касаясь зубами нижней губы; это не русское «в».

questions.question: Who was Charles Babbage?
questions.answer: An inventor who built a mechanical calculator.

questions.question: What did Ada do in 1843?
questions.answer: She translated an article and added her own notes.

questions.question: What did she predict about machines?
questions.answer: They might create music or art.
